issues.message: Requirements define Administrator as a user role, but database schema lacks an 'administrators' table similar to 'patients' and 'doctors' tables. Only the users.role field references administrators without dedicated admin-specific data storage.
Feature F3 (Doctor Schedule Management) is high priority, but design document contains no screens for doctors to set availability or view their schedules. Only patient-facing screens are designed.
Administrator is defined as a user role with system management capabilities, but no administrative interface screens are included in the design document.
No explicit non-functional requirements (NFRs) defined for performance, security, scalability, availability, data retention, backup/recovery, or compliance (e.g., HIPAA for medical data).
Design shows doctor ratings (4.8, 4.9 stars) prominently displayed, but database schema has no table to store ratings, reviews, or feedback from patients.
Design extensively uses user profile photos (96px circles, 64px circles, etc.), but database schema has no field in users, patients, or doctors tables to store profile photo URLs or file references.

Requirements specify 'email and SMS notifications', but notifications table lacks fields for delivery_method (email/sms/push), delivery_status (sent/failed/pending), or delivery_timestamp to track actual delivery.
No unique constraint or mechanism to prevent double-booking of the same doctor at the same date/time. Multiple appointments could be scheduled for identical time slots.
Assumptions mention timezone support, but no timezone field exists in users table or appointments table. Critical for multi-timezone hospital systems or telemedicine.
Appointment status includes 'rescheduled', but no history or audit table exists to track who made changes, when, and what the previous values were. Important for compliance and dispute resolution.
Technical requirements specify both 'Web' and 'Mobile' platforms, but design document only addresses mobile (iOS/Android) with no web-specific responsive design considerations.
No deleted_at or is_deleted fields for soft deletion. Hard deletes could cause referential integrity issues and loss of historical data for appointments and users.

required_fixes: Add 'administrators' table to database schema with admin-specific fields (permissions, department, etc.) or document why it's not needed
Design complete doctor interface screens including schedule management, appointment viewing, and patient details access
Design administrator interface screens for user management, system configuration, and reporting

Define comprehensive non-functional requirements covering performance (response times, concurrent users), security (authentication, authorization, data encryption), scalability, availability (uptime SLA), and compliance (HIPAA, GDPR)
Add 'ratings' or 'reviews' table to database schema with fields: id, doctor_id, patient_id, rating (1-5), review_text, created_at
Add 'profile_photo_url' field to users table (VARCHAR(500), nullable) to support profile images shown in design
Extend notifications table with delivery_method (VARCHAR(20)), delivery_status (VARCHAR(50)), and delivered_at (TIMESTAMP) fields
Add unique constraint on appointments table for (doctor_id, appointment_date, appointment_time) to prevent double-booking, or implement application-level locking
Add 'timezone' field to users table (VARCHAR(50), default 'UTC') to properly handle multi-timezone scenarios
recommendations: Consider adding an appointment_history or audit_log table to track all changes to appointments (original values, new values, changed_by, changed_at) for compliance and dispute resolution
Implement soft delete pattern by adding 'deleted_at' (TIMESTAMP, nullable) fields to critical tables (users, appointments, doctors) to preserve data integrity and enable recovery
Add a 'doctor_unavailability' or 'schedule_exceptions' table to handle one-time schedule changes (vacations, conferences, emergencies) that override regular weekly schedules
Consider adding a 'specializations' reference table instead of free-text in doctors.specialization to enable better filtering, standardization, and multi-specialization support
Add email_verified and phone_verified boolean fields to users table with verification_token field to implement secure account verification flows
Design web-responsive layouts in addition to mobile screens, considering desktop viewport sizes (1024px+, 1440px+) with multi-column layouts and expanded navigation
Include error states and edge cases in design (network errors, booking conflicts, session timeouts, validation errors) with specific error messages and recovery actions
Add created_by and updated_by fields (UUID references to users) in appointments and other transactional tables for better audit trails
Consider implementing a notification_preferences table to allow users to customize which notifications they receive and through which channels (email/SMS/push)
Add indexes on frequently queried timestamp fields (appointments.created_at, notifications.sent_at) and consider composite indexes for common query patterns
